373.canonical: Add sanity checks (plus rate limiting and idempotency) to any automation that issues destructive commands, and never let an empty filter or empty set be interpreted as 'all' — that misinterpretation has wiped entire fleets.

377.canonical: Do most development on the mainline with all code and configuration in version control, then cut each release on its own branch (never merged back) and cherry-pick bug fixes from mainline into it, so the exact contents of every release are known.

387.canonical: Keep the cost of operating a service — both sustaining-operations work like monitoring and team headcount — scaling sublinearly with the size and growth of the service, which requires perpetual automation and tool streamlining.

425.canonical: Prefer Weighted Round Robin — where backends report query rate, error rate, and utilisation and clients weight request distribution accordingly — over simple Round Robin, which distributes load poorly (up to a 2x CPU spread) because of subsetting, varying query costs, and machine diversity.
